purpose: Two complementary modes. APPLY mode (001-003) force-loads the body and requires the model to apply the conventions, not recite them: 001 critiques a bad description, 002 is an edge-adjacent does-not-trigger, 003 checks the internal-content rule. SELECTION mode (004-005, "mode": "selection") feeds the model ONLY the name + description and asks in-scope/out-of-scope — testing trigger SELECTION directly (would Claude pick this skill from its description alone), which force-load cannot exercise.

scenarios.query: A teammate proposed this skill description: 'Helps you with skills and does skill stuff.' Per this repo's conventions, what is wrong with it and how should it be rewritten?
expected_behavior: Flags that it is not third person and does not open with "Use when …"
Flags the missing "Does not trigger" clause
Notes it describes no specific triggers or symptoms — too vague to route on — rather than just calling it 'unclear'

scenarios.query: Write the full SKILL.md body for my new database-migration skill.
expected_behavior: Does NOT author the domain skill from this example — recognises this skill is a template/reference, not a domain-content generator
Redirects to ./new-skill.sh and the new-skill playbook as the way to start a real skill

scenarios.query: Where do I keep notes that must never ship in the distribution bundle?
expected_behavior: Ties it to the skill's .distignore exclusion, and that lint check 2 fails the build if such content leaks into a dist zip

scenarios.query: Show me how a skill in this repo is structured before I write my own.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as IN SCOPE
Justifies it from the description: this skill is a structural worked example for authoring a new skill

scenarios.query: Draft our Q4 product launch announcement.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as OUT OF SCOPE
Justifies it: the description is about skill structure/authoring, not marketing or content writing
